body:
m1 - Rule 3 has now caught three real breaks (laws on the population candidate, embedBench on mine, codec on mine) and every one of them got through because the rule depends on a human remembering to grep. I mechanised it and TESTED IT AGAINST THE ACTUAL FAILURES. It catches all three, and it also finds the module your own count missed.

THE RULE AS TWO COMMANDS. Types defined in the changed files:

  for f in $(git diff --name-only BASE..HEAD | grep '\.scala$'); do
    git show HEAD:$f | grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(final )?(sealed )?(case )?(class|trait|object|enum) [A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*' | awk '{print $NF}'
  done | sort -u

Then, for each type, the modules that reference it:

  for m in $(ls -d */ | sed 's#/##' | grep -vE '^(project|target|docs|amr)$'); do
    grep -rqsw "TYPE" "$m/src" && echo "$m"
  done

RETRODICTION, run just now on the real commits:

  4383a85 (my recall text-span law) defines RecallGraph
    -> align codec embed-bench fixtures interview laws recall   [SEVEN]
    I gated five. The two it names that I missed are exactly codec and embed-bench.

  a9fd20f (my chronology migration) defines RecallSignature (among others)
    -> align embed-bench fixtures   [THREE]
    Names embedBench, which you caught. Also names FIXTURES, which is the third
    module I flagged earlier - so the mechanical rule corrects "exactly TWO"
    without anyone having to remember that it was wrong.

So it would have prevented both of my breaks and would have flagged the laws gap on the population candidate the same way.

LIMITS, stated rather than discovered by whoever trusts it:
- It over-approximates. It lists every module referencing ANY type defined in a changed file, which is usually more than strictly necessary. That is the safe direction and I would not tighten it.
- It sees NAMES, so a reference reached only through a type alias, or a wildcard import where the name is never written, will not be found. I have not looked for such a case in this repo; I am flagging it as unverified rather than claiming coverage.
- It says nothing about RUNTIME consumers whose break is not a compile error - codec's failure was an ExceptionInInitializerError. But it names the module, and running that module's tests is what surfaces it. Naming the module is the whole job.
- It is textual, not semantic. It is a checklist generator, not a proof.

I have NOT put it in the repo. There is no scripts/ directory and adding a top-level one is a structural decision that is yours, not mine. The file is in my scratchpad; say the word and I will land it wherever you want it, or fold the two commands into AGENTS.md rule 3 as the definition of the rule, which I would slightly prefer - a rule stated as a command cannot go stale the way "exactly TWO modules" did.

I am holding off further signature.scala commits until you land the stack, per your do-NOT-re-cut instruction. Corrected head is 1b51be9 and its full-gate counts are on the bead.
